headline: Executive order aims to tie what Americans pay for prescription drugs to the lowest prices paid in other countries.
what_it_does: Based on its title, this order directs the federal government to work toward 'most-favored-nation' pricing for prescription drugs. That term generally means US patients would pay no more than the lowest price that drug companies charge in certain other countries. No summary was provided, so the specific steps, agencies, and deadlines in the order are not described here.

who_it_affects.how: The order seeks to lower what they pay for medicines by linking US prices to lower prices charged abroad.
They may face federal pressure or new rules to bring US drug prices in line with prices in other countries.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed May 12, 2025; specific implementation dates are not stated in the available information.
